channel.title: Acme: Daily Reading List
channel.description: Noteworthy articles from across the web.

item.title: Clover Press revives Marvel Masterworks
item.description: Clover Press is bringing back Marvel Masterworks with new restorations, three cover choices per volume and collectible extras. A Kickstarter launches the line with Uncanny X-Men Vol. 18, Super-Villain Team-Up Vol. 1, The Mighty Thor Vol. 25 and The Tomb of Dracula Vol. 6. Longtime Marvel editor Cory Sedlmeier remains series steward.

item.title: Podium acquisition shows the value of indie authors
item.description: Flexpoint Ford and Shamrock Capital acquired audiobook-focused Podium Entertainment, whose 15,000-title catalog emphasizes genre fiction and authors who began by self-publishing. Podium first drew attention by producing the audiobook of Andy Weir's The Martian. The new owners also plan an employee ownership program.

item.title: Jacksonville library opens a century of newspapers online
item.description: Jacksonville Public Library has expanded free online access to three local newspaper archives: the Florida Times-Union from 1883 to today, the Beaches Leader from 1963 and the Jacksonville Journal from 1901 to 1988. Cardholders can search full pages, photos, cartoons and ads—rich primary material for local history and genealogy.

item.title: Major software firms pledge more support for public package registries
item.description: GitHub, Google, IBM, Microsoft and Sonatype have joined an OpenSSF pledge to help fund package registries such as Maven Central, npm and PyPI. These lightly staffed services handle trillions of downloads while facing rising security and infrastructure costs. The plan targets enterprise customers while keeping access free for developers and small organizations.

item.title: Kim Stanley Robinson keeps returning to the hardest chapter of his climate novel
item.description: Kim Stanley Robinson has discussed The Ministry for the Future in more than 600 talks, but he still will not read its harrowing opening heat-wave chapter aloud. The 74-year-old science-fiction author explains why he set the scene in India, responds to criticism of the novel and describes the persistence behind his guarded optimism.

item.title: Jacksonville lands among Oxford Economics' five U.S. cities to watch
item.description: Oxford Economics named Jacksonville one of five U.S. cities to watch, citing its fast growth, transportation links, business climate and expanding finance, logistics and technology sectors. The assessment also flags familiar pressures: infrastructure, housing affordability and the need for enough skilled workers to sustain the city's momentum.

item.title: WordPress now screens every plugin release before distribution
item.description: Every WordPress.org plugin and theme release now waits through a six-hour cooldown while several models and Jetpack Scan check its changes. High-risk releases are blocked and committers receive the findings. The system already stopped a backdoored update from reaching about 20,000 installations.

item.title: EU vulnerability reporting is now live for digital products
item.description: Manufacturers must now use ENISA's Single Reporting Platform to report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents under the Cyber Resilience Act. The clock is tight: an early warning is due within 24 hours and a fuller notice within 72. Open-source software stewards join the rules in December 2027.

item.title: The case for home-cooked software and barefoot developers
item.description: Maggie Appleton imagines small, inexpensive programs built for a person, family or community rather than a mass market. Her essay connects that “home-cooked” model to local-first software, arguing that ownership, privacy and control matter when people build tools for needs too narrow to interest a large company.

item.title: New laws reopen claims to Nazi-looted art in two museums
item.description: Changes in California and federal law have revived restitution cases involving Lucas Cranach the Elder's “Adam and Eve” at the Norton Simon Museum and watercolors painted at Auschwitz by Dinah Babbitt, now held by Poland's Auschwitz-Birkenau State Museum.

item.title: WordPress 7.1 expands styling, media workflows and Notes
item.description: WordPress 7.1 “Mary Lou” adds new styling controls, smoother media workflows and expanded Notes for collaboration. The official release overview highlights both creator-facing improvements and under-the-hood refinements, making it a useful guide before upgrading production sites.

item.title: Betty Boop, Blondie and three famous detectives enter the public domain
item.description: The 2026 public-domain class includes the earliest Betty Boop and Blondie appearances, plus Nancy Drew, Sam Spade and Miss Marple. Works from 1930 also bring fresh reuse possibilities for Mickey Mouse cartoons, classic songs and films after their U.S. copyright terms expired.

item.title: Lucas Museum opens with comics, Star Wars and fine art under one roof
item.description: After 17 years of planning, George Lucas and Mellody Hobson's $1 billion Museum of Narrative Art is opening in Los Angeles. Its deliberately broad collection puts comic and popular art beside Frida Kahlo, Diego Rivera and Banksy, with Star Wars models, a Naboo starfighter and even the dogs-playing-poker painting among the highlights.

item.title: A WooCommerce plugin flaw is under active attack
item.description: Attackers are exploiting an arbitrary file-upload flaw in the Wholesale Lead Capture Plugin for WooCommerce, which has more than 20,000 installations. The bug can permit unauthenticated PHP webshell uploads. Users should update to version 2.0.3.2 or later and inspect upload directories for unfamiliar PHP files.

item.title: An archaeologist argues for the value of messy digital fragments
item.description: William Caraher revisits “slow” and “punk” archaeology ahead of a conference on the digital, archaeological and ethical. His argument for fragments, ambiguity and incomplete records pushes back against tidy digital systems that can erase the uncertainty and human context that make historical evidence meaningful.
